newsitem.title: ITALY: Deal at hand in Italy metalworker dispute - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Deal at hand in Italy metalworker dispute - Minister.

text.p: All the elements are in place for a resolution to the long-running Italian metalworkers' and engineering dispute, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Monday.

Trade unions representing some 1.7 million metal and engineering workers have already staged two one-day strikes to press their claim for higher wages and union officials have threatened to spread the dispute to other sectors.

The government intervened in the row earlier this month, organising separate meetings with unions and management to try to broker a deal. Treu told reporters at a union convention in this northern town that fresh talks would be held on Tuesday.

"We will start with split talks, but then if we see some signs (of compromise), we will see them together," Treu said. "By now all the elements are in place. If the willingness is there we can close the negotiations," he added.
Contracts in the sector, which accounts for about 40 percent of total manufacturing output in Italy, expired in June and management and unions have so far failed to agree on new terms.
At the heart of the quarrel lies a landmark 1993 wage accord which scrapped automatic index-linked salary increases.
The metalworkers' pay talks are likely to set the standard for wage rounds currently under discussion in a number of other industrial and manufacturing sectors.
